newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Garment maker fined for false labels.
newsitem.headline: Garment maker fined for false labels.

text.p: A court Friday fined a garment manufacturer for affixing "Made in Hong Kong" labels to Chinese-made textile products before shipping them to the United States, the government said.
The court fined the manufacturer HK$398,004 ($51,488) for making a false statement regarding the origin of goods, the government said. It did not name the manufacturer.
The maximum penalty for making a false statement is a HK$500,000 ($64,683) fine and two years in prison.

In June last year U.S. Customs imposed rules requiring Hong Kong textile exporters to provide additional import documentation on a number of textile products in an attempt to stop illegal trans-shipments passing from China through Hong Kong to the United States.
Washington says manufacturers in China are dodging quota limits by sewing in false "Made in Hong Kong" labels.
On Thursday, the U.S. Consulate General said the U.S. Customs Service had sent a delegation to Hong Kong to evaluate the effectiveness of efforts to detect and prevent illegal trans-shipments.
The team's findings will be one factor in U.S. Customs' expected review of the additional import requirements imposed last year, the Consulate General said.
The Hong Kong government said last month it would allow U.S. officials to join its customs officers on inspections of the territory's textiles factories in a bid to resolve the row.
